correctness.rationale: The independent Gaussian constant δ and isotropic first harmonic give |δ|<=tR for two zeros and short gap Δ=2 arccos(|δ|/(tR)). Uniform random direction in R^3 gives exact finite N=1 CDF 1−cos(d/2)*sqrt(1+t²)/sqrt(1+t²cos²(d/2)). For ω→∞, the normalized higher-harmonic amplitude and derivative sums S+D have uniformly-in-N moments O(q), q=e^(−πω/2), because wk/w1<=(1+q²)kq^(k−1). Conditioning on the rare zero-event δ/t in an interval of length ≈2R produces size-bias of Rayleigh R to Maxwell density sqrt(2/π)r²e^(−r²/2) and independent uniform normalized offset V∈[−1,1], uniform first phase, in total variation O(q+t²). C1 stability of simple sinusoidal zeros then transfers to P(Z=2|Z>=1)→1 and CDF(Δ)→1−cos(d/2), uniformly in every finite N(ω). Exact stationarity under phase rotations makes the shorter-arc midpoint uniform and gap-independent on Z=2. I checked all conditional normalizations and C1 tail estimates against the actual proof; the package verify.py checks finite examples but cannot prove the uniform all-N assertion.
